【 PICTURES IN CLINICAL MEDICINE 】
Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Presenting with Alien Hand
Sae Ueda 1,2, Noriko Arai 1, Yuji Kato 1 and Satoshi Suda 1
Key words: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, alien hand, SPECT, DaTscan
(Intern Med 64: 1773-1774, 2025)
(DOI: 10.2169/internalmedicine.4315-24)
A 73-year-old man developed dressing apraxia, lefthemispace neglect, and involuntary levitation of the left upper limb (alien hand, posterior phenotype). Diffusionweighted magnetic resonance imaging showed high-signal
lesions predominantly in the right cerebral cortex (Picture 1A), which became clearly visible after 30 days (Picture 1B). Single-photon emission computed tomography
with iodine-123 iodoamphetamine revealed asymmetric hypoperfusion, predominantly in the right frontal and parietal
regions (Picture 1C), and DaTscan showed reduced uptake
in the right dorsal striatum (Picture 2). Electroencephalography revealed a generalized periodic synchronous discharge
(Picture 3). A cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed the presence of 14-3-3 protein, elevated total tau protein, and a positive real-time quaking-induced conversion test result. Alien
hand persisted for 2 months after the onset, and the patient
developed akinetic mutism 3 months after onset. The patient’s clinical course was consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob
disease (CJD).
CJD rarely presents with an alien hand in its early
stages (1). Multimodal neuroimaging suggests that the alien
hand is probably due to dysfunction of the cortical-striatalthalamic circuitry.
The authors state that they have no Conflict of Interest (COI).
